backtest_12.methodology_explanation: Evaluated using strictly causal rolling-origin time-series cross-validation across 3 historical forecast origins (36 total out-of-sample months, horizon = 12 months). At each origin, models are trained exclusively on prior academic years and evaluated on the subsequent unseen period. Random train/test splitting is never used.

trends_all.causation_disclaimer: These relationships are statistical associations, not evidence of causation.
trends_all.reporting_practice_note: Important Interpretation Note: Increases in recorded safeguarding concerns may reflect changes in student awareness, pastoral accessibility, staff training, or digital recording practices rather than increases in underlying harm. Low forecasted demand in quieter months must never be used to justify reducing statutory safeguarding cover.
key_findings: Pronounced Term-Time Seasonality: Recorded safeguarding concerns peak in Jan (average 219 concerns/month, seasonal index 1.50x) and reach their lowest level in Aug (38 concerns/month, 0.26x).
Multi-Year Demand Trajectory: Across 6 academic years (2020/21 to 2025/26), annual recorded volume moved from 1,435 to 2,067 (+44.0%), while rate per 1,000 students shifted from 205.0 to 270.4.
Reporting Practice Sensitivity: Shifts in recorded volume after September 2023 align with enhanced digital safeguarding workflow adoption and mandatory staff awareness training.

annual_summary.calibration_method: Covariance-calibrated multi-month aggregation (AR(1) error correlation rho=0.10; accounts for cross-month error cancellation rather than summing monthly bounds)

baseline_annual_summary.calibration_method: Covariance-calibrated multi-month aggregation (AR(1) error correlation rho=0.10; accounts for cross-month error cancellation rather than summing monthly bounds)

planning_insights: The Seasonal Naive model forecasts highest recorded safeguarding demand during October (264 concerns) and November (254 concerns), aligning with term-time intake and post-holiday pastoral disclosure patterns.

Over the 12-month horizon (2026/27), total recorded demand is projected at 2,067 concerns (80% calibrated planning range: 1,883 to 2,251), representing an increase of 0.0% (+0 concerns) compared with the prior 12-month period (2,067).
EPYP accounts for the largest share of forecasted demand at 63.1% (1,305 concerns; 371.4 per 1,000 enrolled learners).
'Mental health and wellbeing concerns' remains the primary forecasted category at 41.1% (849 predicted concerns), informing pastoral & mental health specialist triage capacity.

model_accuracy_summary.explanation: Historical 12-month rolling backtest MAE: 27.9 concerns/month (WAPE: 17.1% across 36 out-of-sample months).

scenario_capabilities.enrolment_explanation: Seasonal Naive repeats prior-year monthly counts directly and does not adjust for student population growth.
scenario_capabilities.teaching_days_explanation: Seasonal Naive uses only historical monthly counts and does not incorporate teaching-day changes.
scenario_capabilities.attendance_explanation: Seasonal Naive is a univariate benchmark and does not use attendance rates.
